subject: math

objective.text: Draw a line plot for a data set. Answer questions and draw conclusions from measurement data.

explanations.title: Start at zero with slashes
explanations.text: Write 0 at the start of the scale. Add two slashes after it. The slashes show that the numbers before the first label are not shown. Then label up to the greatest measurement.

explanations.title: Label the unit
explanations.text: Label the scale with the unit of the measuring tool. Look at the table to find the unit. Then put an X above the number for each measurement.

explanations.title: Thermometer
explanations.text: A thermometer is a tool that measures temperature. We measure temperature in degrees. The numbers on a thermometer go up and down.

explanations.title: Vertical line plot
explanations.text: A line plot can have a vertical scale. Then the number line goes up and down. The X's go next to the numbers, in a row. The data stay the same.

explanations.title: When a table is easier
explanations.text: A line plot is easy to read when the numbers are close together. When the numbers are far apart, a table can be easier.

explanations.title: Make the next hundred
explanations.text: To add, make the next hundred first. Move some from the second number to the first. Then add what is left.

hints.text: Think about how many more make the next hundred.
Make 10 tens first. Then add the tens that are left.
Look at the smallest and the greatest numbers in the table.
The longest row or tallest stack of X's is the most common.
Subtract the smallest measurement from the greatest.
Add the number of X's at every measurement.
Think about the numbers before the first label.
Draw a tape diagram. Find the cost of the first item, then add.
Look at where the numbers are. Think about why they are there.
Think about when you are sick, or about the weather outside.

assets_required.why_this_method: Exact X counts and number labels need exact behaviour. Diffusion cannot count X's, keep equal spacing or draw a vertical scale reliably.
assets_required.description: A number line with X's above or next to the numbers, a title and a unit label. It can be horizontal with a zero and two slashes, or vertical like a thermometer.
must_show_exactly: Zero, two slashes, then the first label when asked
One X per measurement, same size
Vertical version has X's in rows
states_or_frames: Pencil box plot from 6 to 17 cm
Vertical temperature plot from 59 to 72 degrees
Number line with two slashes after zero
assets_required.interaction: Tutor sets the numbers and X counts from the stimulus. Child can place an X. Child answers by voice or typing.
assets_required.alt_text: A line plot with X's above or beside a number line.
assets_required.generation_caption: Line plot, X's on a number line, labeled units, plain white background. [Build by code]

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
